## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṇṇikajātaka* (Ja 102), translated as *The Greengrocer*, is a birth-story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection. The frame story takes place at Jetavana, where the Buddha recounts the narrative regarding a lay disciple from Sāvatthī who earned his living as a greengrocer selling diverse roots, vegetables, and pumpkins. The greengrocer had a daughter who was both virtuous and pretty, but who laughed constantly; when a marriage proposal was made by a family of equal standing, the father resolved to test her chastity beforehand to ensure she would not bring disgrace upon her parents.

Having tested her and heard her declare that she had successfully preserved her virtue, the father escorted her home, celebrated the wedding, and sent her to her new family [Fausböll 1877]. Following this account, the Buddha expounds the Four Noble Truths, leading the lay greengrocer to attain the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1877]. In the birth-story's identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that the father and daughter were the same individuals in both lifetimes, whereas he himself was the tree deity (*rukkhadevatā*) who had observed the test directly [Fausböll 1877].
